html:
SMTO-POL-0016 — A step needed a result from an earlier step that didn't finish

GUID: 1fa5fbf9-d5fe-425c-84b8-4954ca9af923
Slug: input-receipt-guard
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • The Agent tried to pass the output of an earlier step into a new one, but SMTO has no complete, successful result for that earlier step. The new step didn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the task in the conversation and look at its tool calls to find the earlier step this one relied on, and whether it failed or never ran. The new step can only use a result from a step that finished successfully in this task.
  2. If that earlier step was meant to change something, such as writing a file, check that file or item yourself. A failed or unfinished step may still have changed something, and repeating it could do it twice.
  3. Reply asking the Agent to run the earlier step again only if it didn't happen, and then to continue. A fresh, successful result gives the next step the input it needs.

What success looks like

  • The earlier step shows a successful result, and the step that needed it runs.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Then select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off Agent Checks to get past this; the step would run without the data it needs.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Input binding resolution rejected a source_operation_id whose receipt is missing, failed, unexecuted or incomplete in this run's scope (execution.input_receipts), so the tool call that depended on it was not executed.

What this means

  • A bound input must resolve to a complete, executed, successful or valid completed-process receipt in the owning run; missing or incomplete evidence cannot supply trusted input. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • A bound input must resolve to a complete, executed, successful or valid completed-process receipt in the owning run; missing or incomplete evidence cannot supply trusted input.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact receipt reference, completion/execution flags and supported binding pointer within the owning run.

How to fix it

  • Look up the referenced source_operation_id in the run's results and receipt store (execution/bindings.py resolve_bindings) and confirm it executed, completed and succeeded, or is a valid completed-process result. Re-run the producing step only after checking its effects, then bind with the exact new operation ID and a valid JSON Pointer; do not fabricate receipts or disable the execution.input_receipts check.
  • Use exact observed receipt identities and supported binding pointers. Do not fabricate a receipt or replay a mutation to satisfy an input binding.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Every bound value comes from its authoritative eligible receipt and valid pointer.

What not to do

  • Do not disable the guard as a routine remedy.
  • Do not substitute a different timeout, permission or model setting for this control.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
